mainTopic: Collecting a debt through a messenger, and whether a robber's heirs must pay the חומש
overview: The amud opens with שמואל's ruling that a debtor may not pay a messenger who only shows the creditor's personal sign (דיוקני), even if witnesses signed it. רבי יוחנן allows it when witnesses are signed. Following שמואל, the story of רבי אבא and רבא shows that a receipt (התקבלתי) is not enough, because the creditor might die and the debt would pass to his heirs. The real fix is to transfer the debt to the messenger through land (קנין אגב קרקע), as רב פפא did. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and proves from several sources that חומש is ממון, so יורשין must pay it. A ברייתא seems to say the opposite: the heir is free of חומש because he did not rob, though he does pay the קרן. רב נחמן answers that the sources differ over whether the robber admitted. After pushback, the גמרא explains the case as one where the father did not admit but the son did, the stolen item is gone, and the father left land. The amud ends with a new problem: a debt like this is an oral loan (מלוה על פה), which cannot be collected from heirs. The answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: A creditor's sign is not enough to send money
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a debtor may not pay a messenger who only shows the creditor's personal sign, even if witnesses signed on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A debtor may not send money through someone just because that person carries the creditor's sign, even if witnesses are signed on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states שמואל's ruling: a messenger holding the creditor's personal mark is not trusted to collect the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sign alone does not prove that the creditor actually appointed this person as his agent. Even witnesses who confirm that the sign is the creditor's do not fix the problem. If the money is lost on the way, the debtor would still owe it.

keyTerms.meaning: a personal figure or sign used in place of a signature

phrases.english: One may not send money on the basis of a sign-figure,
phrases.notes: The creditor's personal mark, handed to the messenger as if to say 'I sent him.'

phrases.english: and even if witnesses are signed on it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, a דיוקני does not make someone an agent for collecting a debt, even with witnesses.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן allows it when witnesses are signed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: if witnesses are signed on the sign, the debtor may send the money with the messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: if witnesses are signed on it, one may send the money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי יוחנן's opposing view, which allows paying the messenger when witnesses are signed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, signed witnesses are strong enough proof that the creditor really appointed the messenger. The two opinions disagree only about the case with witnesses. Without witnesses, both agree the sign is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: the great אמורא of ארץ ישראל who disagrees with שמואל here

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן says:
If witnesses are signed on it, one may send.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes שמואל's ruling for the case where witnesses are signed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, a דיוקני with signed witnesses is enough to send money.

steps.title: What can a creditor do according to שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what solution a far-away creditor has if שמואל does not accept a sign with witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: according to שמואל, what is the fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a practical question, and this sets up the story that follows: if a sign does not work, how can a creditor collect without travelling himself?
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's strict rule seems to leave a creditor stuck. The גמרא wants a method that gives the debtor full protection.

phrases.english: They said: According to שמואל, what is the fix?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A workable way to collect a debt through a messenger according to שמואל.

steps.title: רבי אבא's messenger and the first idea: a receipt
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא sent רב ספרא to collect his money from רב יוסף בר חמא. The debtor's son רבא first demanded a written receipt from רבי אבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רבי אבא, who was owed money by רב יוסף בר חמא. He told רב ספרא, 'When you come back, bring the money to me.' When רב ספרא went there, רבא, the debtor's son, asked him, 'Did he write you an "I have received"?' He said, 'No.' רבא answered, 'Then go first and have him write you an "I have received."'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering with a story. רבא's first suggestion is that רב ספרא should bring a receipt signed by רבי אבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A receipt written by the creditor would protect the debtor: once he pays, he has proof that the debt is settled. This is the first try at a fix. The גמרא will improve on it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: was owed money (literally, 'brought up coins' against someone)

phrases.english: Like that case of רבי אבא,

phrases.aramaic: הָוֵי מַסֵּיק זוּזֵי בִּדְרַב יוֹסֵף בַּר חָמָא,
phrases.english: who was owed money by רב יוסף בר חמא.
He said to רב ספרא:
When you come back, bring it to me.
When he went there,
רבא, his son, said to him:
Did he write you 'I have received'?
He said to him: No.
If so, go first,
and let him write you 'I have received.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא הָוֵי מַסֵּיק זוּזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question of what שמואל's fix is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First idea: the messenger should bring a receipt signed by the creditor.

steps.title: A receipt fails if the creditor dies
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes back his first idea: if רבי אבא dies before the money arrives, the debt belongs to his orphans, and his receipt is worthless.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end he said: even if he writes you 'I have received,' it is nothing. Maybe by the time you come, רבי אבא will have died, the money will pass to the orphans, and רבי אבא's 'I have received' will be nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא knocks down his own suggestion by pointing out a real danger: the creditor might die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The receipt only works if the person who wrote it still owns the debt when the money is paid. If the creditor dies, the debt passes to his heirs (יתמי), and his receipt cannot release a debt that is no longer his. The debtor would then have to pay again.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not arguing with someone else here. He is rejecting his OWN earlier advice from the previous step.

phrases.english: In the end he said to him:
Even if he writes you 'I have received,'
it is nothing;
perhaps by the time you arrive, רבי אבא will have died,
and the money will fall before the orphans,
phrases.notes: He means the debt becomes part of the inheritance owed to his children.

phrases.aramaic: וְ״הִתְקַבַּלְתִּי״ דְּרַבִּי אַבָּא לָאו כְּלוּם הוּא.
phrases.english: and רבי אבא's 'I have received' will be nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְסוֹף אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי כָּתַב לָךְ נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the receipt solution from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a receipt from the creditor fully protects the debtor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the creditor dies before payment, the debt belongs to his heirs, so his receipt cannot release it.

steps.title: Then what is the solution?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks רבא what the real fix is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Then what is the fix?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא asks for a better method, and this sets up רבא's final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the receipt idea failed, the question from step 3 is open again, now framed inside the story.

phrases.english: He said to him: Rather, what is the fix?
phrases.notes: רב ספרא is the one asking.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A method that still works even if the creditor dies.

steps.title: Transfer the debt to the messenger through land
steps.stepSummary: רבא's solution: רבי אבא should transfer the debt to רב ספרא together with land, and then רב ספרא writes the receipt himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Go, have him transfer it to you by means of land, and then you come and write us 'I have received.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the real fix: make the messenger the owner of the debt, so his own receipt is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Through קנין אגב קרקע, the debt is transferred along with a piece of land, so it now belongs to the messenger. If the original creditor dies, it no longer matters, because the debt is not his anymore. The messenger can therefore write a receipt that truly protects the debtor.

keyTerms.meaning: let him transfer ownership of them (the coins)

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the safe way to collect through a messenger is to make the messenger the owner of the debt by קנין אגב קרקע. A sign or a receipt from the creditor is not enough.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the standard method for collecting a debt from far away while fully protecting the debtor.

phrases.english: Go, let him transfer them to you by means of land,
phrases.notes: רבי אבא gives רב ספרא some land, and the debt goes along with it.

phrases.english: and come, you write us 'I have received.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Transfer the debt to the messenger with קנין אגב קרקע, and then the messenger writes the receipt.

steps.title: רב פפא used this method
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא transferred a debt of twelve thousand זוזים in בי חוזאי to רב שמואל בר אבא through the threshold of his house. When the money arrived, he went out to meet him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the case of רב פפא, who was owed twelve thousand זוזים in בי חוזאי. He transferred them to רב שמואל בר אבא together with the threshold of his house. When he came back, רב פפא went out to meet him as far as תואך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real case showing a sage who used the land-transfer method in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a small piece of land, like a doorstep, is enough for the debt to be transferred with it. The story shows that the method worked: the messenger returned with the money. רב פפא's going out to meet him shows how glad he was to receive it.

keyTerms.meaning: a far-off region where the debtor lived

phrases.english: Like that case of רב פפא,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה מַסֵּיק תְּרֵיסַר אַלְפֵי זוּזֵי בֵּי חוֹזָאֵי,
phrases.english: who was owed twelve thousand zuz in בי חוזאי.

phrases.aramaic: אַקְנִינְהוּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ לְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: He transferred them to רב שמואל בר אבא
by means of the threshold of his house.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא, נְפַק לְאַפֵּיהּ עַד תְּוָאךְ.
phrases.english: When he came, he went out toward him as far as תואך.
phrases.notes: רב פפא is the one who went out, to greet the messenger bringing the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב פָּפָּא הֲוָה מַסֵּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the קנין אגב קרקע solution with a real-life case.
steps.raayaObject: The method of transferring a debt to a messenger through land.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of רב פפא and רב שמואל בר אבא.

steps.title: From the משנה: the fifth is real money, so heirs pay it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about returning the קרן without the חומש and concludes that חומש is ממון, so יורשין must pay it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he gave him the principal (but not the fifth, he does not need to chase after him). This shows the fifth is money owed, and if the robber dies, his heirs pay it to the victim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and draws a rule from it: the חומש is a money debt, so the robber's יורשין must pay it if he dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats a missing חומש like a regular money debt, since it does not require the special effort of chasing after the victim. A regular money debt passes on to heirs. So the גמרא concludes that יורשין pay the חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: The principal, meaning the value of the stolen item itself
The extra fifth a robber adds after swearing falsely
Money, meaning a real money debt and not a fine or penalty

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether חומש is ממון decides whether it passes to heirs. The rest of this section is built on that question.

phrases.english: If he gave him the principal, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה here. The rest of that line says he does not have to chase after the victim to give him the fifth.

phrases.english: Apparently, the fifth is a money debt,
and if he dies, the heirs pay it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן לוֹ אֶת הַקֶּרֶן וְכוּ׳. אַלְמָא חוֹמֶשׁ מָמוֹנָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the debt-agent stories and goes back to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חומש is ממון, so יורשין must pay it

steps.title: Second proof: a fifth is added on top of a fifth
steps.stepSummary: Another line of the משנה says that someone who swore falsely about the חומש adds a new חומש on top of it. This again shows that חומש is ממון.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned in the משנה: if he gave the principal and swore falsely about the fifth, he adds a fifth on top of the fifth. This shows the fifth is a money debt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings more support from the משנה. If you swear falsely about the חומש itself, you owe another חומש on top of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swearing falsely about a debt creates a new חומש. If swearing about the חומש creates a new one, then the חומש must count as a money debt. That supports the conclusion of step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: And we also learned in a משנה
He adds a fifth on top of the fifth

phrases.english: And we also learned:
If he gave the principal
and swore falsely about the fifth,
phrases.notes: He falsely swore that he had already paid the fifth.

phrases.english: he adds a fifth on top of the fifth.
Apparently, the fifth is a money debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof from the משנה for step 9's conclusion
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: one who swore falsely about the חומש adds a חומש on top of the חומש

steps.title: Third proof: a ברייתא says heirs pay the fifth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says outright that if a robber swore falsely and died, his יורשין pay the קרן and the חומש but do not bring the אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: one who robbed his fellow, swore to him falsely, and then died, his heirs pay the principal and the fifth, but they are exempt from bringing the guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says clearly what steps 9 and 10 only implied: heirs pay the חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא separates the money payments from the קרבן. The heirs pay the קרן and חומש because these are money debts. They do not bring the אשם, which was the father's own atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was also taught this way in a ברייתא
A guilt-offering brought for a false oath about money

steps.whatToRemember: Three sources so far say that חומש is ממון and that יורשין pay it.

phrases.english: And it was also taught this way:

phrases.aramaic: הַגּוֹזֵל אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ, וְנִשְׁבַּע לוֹ, וָמֵת –
phrases.english: One who robs his fellow, swears to him falsely, and dies:
the heirs pay the principal and the fifth,
but they are exempt from the guilt-offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא that states the rule outright
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: heirs of a robber who swore falsely pay קרן and חומש but are exempt from the אשם

steps.title: Challenge: another ברייתא limits when heirs pay the fifth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether heirs really pay their father's חומש, and contrasts the sources above with a ברייתא saying an heir does not pay חומש for his father's robbery when no one swore.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do heirs really have to pay their father's fifth, as if the fifth is money and heirs must pay it? Contrast this with a ברייתא: I still say, when does he not pay a fifth for his father's robbery? When neither he nor his father swore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the conclusion it just built and sets up a contradiction from another ברייתא. That ברייתא continues in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new ברייתא first raises the thought that an heir might be free of חומש for his father's robbery only when nobody swore. In the next step it asks about the cases where someone did swear, and it frees the heir there too. That clashes with the sources saying heirs pay חומש because it is ממון.

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast them, meaning here is a source that seems to contradict
I still say, meaning I add a further point

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not finished here. Its ending comes in step 13, and רב נחמן answers the contradiction in step 14.

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹרְשִׁין בְּנֵי שַׁלּוֹמֵי חוּמְשָׁא דַּאֲבוּהוֹן הָווּ –
phrases.english: But are heirs obligated to pay their father's fifth?
Apparently the fifth is a money debt,
and heirs must pay it.
But contrast them with this:
I still say:
phrases.notes: The ברייתא already said a person pays a fifth only for his own robbery, not his father's. 'I still say' raises a possible limit that the ברייתא goes on to reject.

phrases.english: When does he not pay a fifth
for his father's robbery?

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁבַּע לֹא הוּא וְלֹא אָבִיו;
phrases.english: When neither he nor his father swore;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיוֹרְשִׁין בְּנֵי שַׁלּוֹמֵי חוּמְשָׁא דַּאֲבוּהוֹן הָווּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of steps 9 to 11 using a different ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that יורשין pay their father's חומש because it is ממון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא frees an heir from חומש on his father's robbery, and, as it goes on to say, this holds even when false oaths were taken. That clashes with treating חומש as a money debt that passes to heirs.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: even when someone swore, the heir is free of חומש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its point. Whether the son swore falsely, the father swore falsely, or both did, the heir does not pay חומש, because the פסוק speaks of the one who robbed, and the heir did not rob.
steps.simpleTranslation: What if he swore and not his father, or his father and not he, or both of them? How do we know he is exempt? The פסוק says, "that he robbed" and "that he exploited," and this heir did not rob and did not exploit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from the last step that seems to argue with our משנה. This ending shows that the ברייתא frees the heir from חומש even when false oaths were taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the ברייתא covered the case where nobody swore. Now it widens the rule to every case of a false oath. It bases this on the פסוק's wording: חומש falls on the robber himself, and the heir is not the robber. This makes the clash with the משנה and the earlier ברייתא (step 11) sharp and direct.

keyTerms.meaning: Exploited; held back money that was owed

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא is talking about the חומש only, not the קרן. It never says the heir keeps the stolen item itself.

phrases.english: He swore falsely, but not his father,
his father swore, but not he,
he and his father both swore: from where do we know he is exempt?
The verse says: "that he robbed" and "that he exploited"
and he (the heir) did not rob and did not exploit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא וְלֹא אָבִיו, אָבִיו וְלֹא הוּא, הוּא וְאָבִיו – מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that step 12 began, so the contradiction with steps 9-11 is complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion from the משנה and the ברייתא in step 11 that יורשין pay חומש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This ברייתא uses the פסוק to free the heir from חומש even when false oaths were taken, which seems to clash directly with the sources that make him pay.

steps.title: רב נחמן: it depends on whether the father admitted
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן settles the contradiction. The sources that make the heir pay חומש are talking about a father who admitted. The ברייתא that frees him is talking about a father who never admitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: There is no difficulty. Here he admitted, and here he did not admit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the contradiction by splitting the cases into two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father admitted his false oath while he was alive, he became obligated to pay חומש, and that debt passes to his heirs. If he died without admitting, he never became obligated in חומש, so there is nothing for the heirs to pay. That way both sources are right, each about its own case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said: It is not difficult;
here, where he admitted,
phrases.notes: Meaning the father admitted while he was alive. These are the sources where the heir pays חומש.

phrases.english: here, where he did not admit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא; כָּאן שֶׁהוֹדָה, כָּאן שֶׁלֹּא הוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 12-13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each source is talking about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seem to disagree about whether heirs pay חומש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Heirs pay חומש only if the father admitted. If he never admitted, they do not.

steps.title: If he never admitted, the heir would not pay even the קרן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב נחמן. If the father never admitted, the heir should not pay even the קרן. But the ברייתא only looks for a source to free him from חומש, which shows it holds that he does pay the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not admit, then he would not pay even the קרן! And if you say that is true, he really does not pay it: but since the תנא searches for a source only about חומש, that shows the heir does pay the קרן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב נחמן's answer. A ברייתא about a father who never admitted does not fit, because this ברייתא clearly expects the heir to pay the קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father never admitted, the robbery was never established, so the heir would not pay anything at all. But the ברייתא works hard to find a פסוק that frees him only from חומש. That would make no sense if he were already free of the קרן too. So the ברייתא must be a case where he pays the קרן, which means it cannot be a case of 'did not admit.'

keyTerms.meaning: The principal; the value of what was stolen

phrases.english: If he did not admit,
he would not pay even the principal!

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא: הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא מְשַׁלֵּם;
phrases.english: And if you would say: indeed, he does not pay it;
but from the fact that he (the תנא) searches for a source about the one-fifth,
that is to say that he does pay the principal!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לֹא הוֹדָה, קֶרֶן נָמֵי לָא מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's answer from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that the exempting ברייתא is about a father who did not admit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father never admitted, the heir owes nothing, not even the קרן. Yet the ברייתא only bothers to free him from חומש, which shows it assumes he pays the קרן. So the ברייתא cannot be about a 'did not admit' case.

steps.title: The same ברייתא says the heir pays the קרן in every case
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the ברייתא openly says the heir pays the קרן in every case: when both swore, when only one swore, and when neither swore. It learns this from the four words in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is further taught: I would still say, when does he pay the קרן for his father's robbery? Only when he and his father both swore. If his father swore and not he, or he and not his father, or neither of them, from where do we know? The פסוק says: robbery, exploitation, lost item, and deposit. There is a source to learn from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings more of the same ברייתא as extra proof that it holds the heir pays the קרן. This makes the problem with רב נחמן's answer stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests the heir might pay the קרן only when both he and his father swore. It then uses the four words of the פסוק to teach that he pays the קרן in every case, even when no one swore. A ברייתא that makes the heir pay the קרן this broadly cannot be about a father who never admitted, which was רב נחמן's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: And further, it is taught (in a ברייתא)
And I would still say (a possible thought, about to be rejected)
There is a source to learn from

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next stage of the סוגיא. רב נחמן's distinction cannot mean that no one admitted, so his words will have to be read in a new way (step 19).

phrases.english: And further, it is taught: And I would still say:
phrases.notes: This is the same ברייתא continuing. 'I would still say' brings up a thought that the ברייתא is about to reject.

phrases.english: When does he pay the principal
for his father's robbery?
Only when he and his father both swore falsely.
If his father swore and not he,
he swore and not his father,
or neither he nor his father: from where do we know he pays?
The verse says: "robbery" and "exploitation,"
"lost item" and "deposit":
there is a source to learn from.
phrases.notes: Meaning these words of the פסוק teach that the heir pays the קרן in all these cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, open proof to the challenge in step 15 against רב נחמן.
steps.raayaObject: That the exempting ברייתא holds the heir pays the קרן, so it cannot be about a father who did not admit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuation of the same ברייתא, which learns from the four words of ויקרא 5:23 that the heir pays the קרן in all cases.

steps.title: רבה asks his father exactly what wording he said
steps.stepSummary: While רב הונא was teaching this ברייתא, his son רבה asked whether he had said 'there is a derivation' or 'they will be paid.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא was sitting and teaching this teaching. His son רבה asked him: Did you say 'יש תלמוד' (there is a source in the פסוק), or did you say 'ישתלמו' (they will be paid)?
steps.whatsHappening: A short story about how the ברייתא from Step 16 was taught. רבה asks his father to clear up which words he actually said, and this sets up his father's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two phrases sound almost the same when spoken quickly. רבה wants to know whether the heir's duty to pay the קרן is learned from a פסוק, or is simply stated as a rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling that was taught over
There is a source to learn it from, a derivation from the פסוק
Master, a polite way to address a teacher

phrases.english: And Rav Huna was sitting
and was saying this teaching.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from the step before, which says the heir pays the קרן in every case.

phrases.english: Rabba, his son, said to him:
Is the Master saying 'there is a derivation',
phrases.notes: The two Hebrew phrases sound almost the same out loud, so רבה wasn't sure which one he heard.

phrases.english: or is the Master saying 'they will be paid'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies exactly how the ברייתא in Step 16 was worded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב הונא said 'יש תלמוד' or 'ישתלמו'.

steps.title: רב הונא: there is a derivation from the extra words in the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that he said 'there is a derivation,' and that it comes from the extra words in the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I said 'there is a derivation,' and I am saying it is learned from the extra words in the פסוקים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers his son. The heir's duty to pay the קרן is learned from the extra words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This confirms that the ברייתא really does make the heir pay the קרן, and roots that duty in the פסוק. So רב נחמן's reading, where the father never admitted and the heir pays nothing, still does not fit the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra or widening word in a פסוק that adds cases

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא clearly makes the heir pay the קרן. Any answer to the contradiction has to fit that.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am saying 'there is a derivation',
and I say it from the extra words of the verses.
phrases.notes: He means the four words in the פסוק mentioned in Step 16.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's question from Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is 'יש תלמוד'. The heir pays the קרן, learned from the extra words in the פסוק.

steps.title: New meaning of 'did not admit': the father didn't, but the son did
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets רב נחמן. The father did not admit, but the son did, so the son pays the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'he did not admit' mean? The father did not admit, but his son did admit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rescues רב נחמן's answer by giving his words a new meaning. The case is that the father never admitted, but the son later admitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the son admitted, he owes the קרן, which fits the ברייתא. There is no חומש, because the father, the one who stole, never admitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what does it mean? It opens a new reading

steps.confusionAlert: 'Did not admit' still means the father. The new detail is that the son admitted, and that is why he still pays the קרן.

phrases.english: Rather, what is 'he did not admit'?
His father did not admit,
but his son admitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repairs רב נחמן's answer after the attack in Steps 15 to 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Did not admit' meant nobody admitted, so the heir should pay nothing at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father did not admit, but the son did, so the son pays the קרן and no חומש.

steps.title: Then the son should pay חומש for his own oath
steps.stepSummary: If the son swore falsely and then admitted, he should owe חומש for his own oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let the son be obligated to pay חומש because of his own oath!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new case. A son who swore falsely and then admitted should owe חומש for his own oath.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא frees the heir from חומש even where the son swore. Yet anyone who swears falsely and then admits normally pays חומש, so the new reading seems to clash with that rule.

phrases.english: But let his son be liable for the one-fifth payment
for his own oath!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case defined in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The new reading: the father did not admit and the son did.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A son who swore falsely and admitted should owe חומש for his own oath, but the ברייתא frees him.

steps.title: The stolen item no longer exists
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the case is where the stolen item is gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: the case is where the stolen item no longer exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the stolen item is no longer around. So the son's oath does not create a חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The son's oath only brings חומש if it was about something he truly owed. If the item is gone, his false oath was not about a debt that obligates חומש.

phrases.english: They say:
It is where the stolen item does not exist.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son swore about an item that still exists, so he owes חומש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The item is gone, so the son's oath does not bring חומש.

steps.title: If the item is gone, he shouldn't pay even the קרן
steps.stepSummary: If the stolen item no longer exists, the heir should not even owe the קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is where the stolen item no longer exists, then he should not pay even the קרן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If the item is gone, the heir should owe nothing at all, but the ברייתא makes him pay the קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heirs return a stolen item that is still there. If it is gone, they normally do not have to pay for it. So the answer from Step 21 now clashes with the ברייתא's rule that the heir pays the קרן.

phrases.english: If it is where the stolen item does not exist,
he should not pay even the principal!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּשֶׁאֵין גְּזֵילָה קַיֶּימֶת, אֲפִילּוּ קֶרֶן נָמֵי לָא מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the stolen item no longer exists.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Heirs do not pay for a stolen item that is gone, yet the ברייתא makes them pay the קרן.

steps.title: The father left land
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the father left land, so the heir pays the קרן from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where there is guaranteed property (land).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the father left land. The heir pays the קרן from that inherited land even though the item itself is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land is the kind of property a debt can be collected from. So the heir can owe the קרן from the land, while there is still no חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for this case
Guaranteed property, meaning land that can be collected from

phrases.english: No, it is needed
where there is guaranteed property.
phrases.notes: He means land the heir inherited from the father who stole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a detail to the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With the item gone, the heir has nothing to pay from.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father left land, so the heir pays the קרן from it.

steps.title: Land doesn't help: this is an oral loan
steps.stepSummary: Even with land, this debt counts as an oral loan, and an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs or buyers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if there is land, so what? It is an oral loan, and an oral loan cannot be collected from the heirs or from buyers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the land answer. A debt like this counts as an oral loan, and that kind of loan cannot be collected from heirs, so the land should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan written in a document can be collected from the land of heirs and buyers. An oral loan cannot. This debt has no document, so it seems the heir should still not have to pay the קרן.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan by spoken agreement, with no document
Buyers, people who bought land from the debtor

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of מלוה על פה, that an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs or buyers, is the barrier any answer here must get past.

phrases.english: And when there is guaranteed property,
what of it?
It is a loan by oral agreement,
phrases.notes: A debt from robbery has no written document, so it is treated like a spoken loan.

phrases.english: and an oral loan cannot be collected
not from the heirs
and not from the buyers!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אִיכָּא אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים מַאי הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that land lets the heir pay the קרן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This debt counts as an oral loan, and an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs, so the land should not help.

steps.title: The Sages begin their reply
steps.stepSummary: The word אמרי opens the גמרא's answer to the problem from step 24: an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say [in response]:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to answer the problem about the oral loan, and the actual answer comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 seemed to break the whole case: the heir pays the קרן from the father's land, but an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs. The word אמרי signals that the Sages are about to explain the case so that this rule does not block it. Nothing new about the law is said yet.

keyTerms.meaning: "They say." A formula that introduces an answer given by the Sages, usually a reply to a problem just raised.
An oral loan, a debt with no written document. This is the problem the answer is responding to.
Heirs, the people who inherit the father's property.
Buyers who purchased land from the debtor.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the answer in this line. אמרי only announces that an answer is coming.

phrases.english: They say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces the response to the problem in step 24, that an oral loan cannot be collected from heirs.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setup formula only. The actual answer follows in the next line.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since this debt is an oral loan, the heir apparently cannot be made to pay the קרן from the father's land.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated. The next line will explain how the case avoids the oral-loan problem.
